historical_commentary.text: This note is a companion troubleshooting guide to TN 96-28, offering more detailed, symptom-specific diagnostic tips for ADSP, IPX, and TCP/IP connection failures between 4D Client and 4D Server circa 1996, including PCI Macintosh Open Transport requirements, zone/Frame Type mismatches, subnet/router misconfiguration, the -10002 timeout error, and a Windows 95 TCP memory leak. As with its companion note, the AppleTalk and IPX protocols discussed are entirely discontinued, and the TCP/IP diagnostic details (manual subnet/router configuration on 1996-era OSes, Windows 95-specific bugs) reflect networking practices and defects that no longer apply to any current system, even though basic principles like using Ping to test connectivity remain valid today.
related_updates: AppleTalk/ADSP and IPX/SPX, the two legacy protocols covered alongside TCP/IP here, have both been fully discontinued for decades
The Windows 95 TCP/IP memory leak and Open Transport PCI Macintosh requirements described are specific historical software defects/requirements with no relevance to any modern OS

Modern network diagnostics rely on the same fundamental tools referenced here (Ping, checking subnet/router configuration) but within vastly different, largely auto-configured (DHCP-based) networking environments
